module.email_security.checks: Analyses the email protection of the domain: SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MTA-STS and TLS-RPT, with an overall grade.
module.email_security.fix:
List every service that sends email with your domain (mail platform, newsletter, CRM, invoicing, printers, applications): missing one would get legitimate messages rejected once the rules are tightened.
In the domain's DNS zone (registrar or DNS host console), publish ONE SINGLE SPF TXT record at the apex that lists those services and ends with `-all` (`~all` only while you roll it out). Examples: `include:_spf.google.com` for Google Workspace, `include:spf.protection.outlook.com` for Microsoft 365. Never `+all`, and at most 10 DNS lookups (`include`, `a`, `mx`, `exists`, `redirect`).
Enable DKIM signing at each sending service and publish the public key it provides (RSA 2048 bits) in a TXT record `selector._domainkey.example.com`, where `selector` is the name the service gives you.
Publish a DMARC TXT record at `_dmarc.example.com`, in monitoring mode first: `v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@example.com`. The `rua` address receives the daily reports from the large mailbox providers.
Read those reports for 2 to 4 weeks and fix every legitimate sender that gets neither SPF nor DKIM aligned with the address shown in the From header.
Then tighten the policy: `p=quarantine`, then `p=reject` as soon as no legitimate sender fails. Remove any `pct=` value below 100 and, if your subdomains do not send email, add `sp=reject`.
A domain that sends no email: publish `v=spf1 -all` as SPF and `p=reject` as DMARC. For encryption of inbound mail, see also the "MTA-STS and TLS-RPT" and "SMTP probe" modules.
Check with `dig +short TXT example.com` and `dig +short TXT _dmarc.example.com`, then send a message to an external mailbox: the `Authentication-Results` header must show `spf=pass`, `dkim=pass` and `dmarc=pass`. Then run the scan again.
module.email_security.fix_snippet:
# DNS SPF
example.com.  IN  TXT  "v=spf1 include:_spf.example.net ip4:203.0.113.10 ip6:2001:db8::1 -all"
# DNS DKIM
selector1._domainkey.example.com.  IN  TXT  "v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=PUBLIC_KEY_FROM_YOUR_SENDING_SERVICE"
# DNS DMARC p=none
_dmarc.example.com.  IN  TXT  "v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@example.com"
# DNS DMARC p=reject
_dmarc.example.com.  IN  TXT  "v=DMARC1; p=reject; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@example.com"
# dig
dig +short TXT example.com
dig +short TXT _dmarc.example.com
dig +short TXT selector1._domainkey.example.com
module.email_security.title: Email security
module.email_security.why: Without SPF and an enforced DMARC policy, anyone can send email on behalf of the domain: phishing, CEO fraud, reputation damage.
